sections.title: So… You’re Here 👀
sections.content:
If you’re reading this, there’s a good chance you’re either a friend, a student, someone curious, or someone who just kept clicking around and ended up here. That’s okay — this profile exists exactly for that reason.

This space is meant to feel informal and fun. It’s a mix of who Shashwat is as a person, what he does professionally (in a very non-serious way), and random things that make him… him. No resumes, no heavy explanations — just a human overview.

Think of this as the part of the website where you’re allowed to scroll aimlessly.

sections.title: What He Does (The Non-Boring Version)
sections.content:
Very briefly — Shashwat works in Applied AI. He builds systems that involve Generative AI, automation, and large-scale platforms. A lot of his work revolves around making AI systems actually useful in the real world instead of just sounding impressive.

On most days, this means designing systems, thinking about how different pieces fit together, breaking things, fixing them, and occasionally wondering why something that worked yesterday is broken today.

If you’re a student: yes, this is the same AI you keep hearing about. And no, it’s not just about prompts. There’s a lot of engineering, math, and debugging involved.

If you’re a friend: yes, this is the thing he keeps talking about when he says “work is interesting these days.”

sections.title: Student Life, College & Figuring Things Out
sections.content:
Shashwat studied at IIT Delhi, which sounds very serious on paper but was also full of hostel life, late nights, friendships, stress, fun, and a lot of figuring things out.

College was where he learned that everyone is good at something, that it’s okay to not have everything figured out, and that growth usually comes with discomfort. There were great days, bad days, and many confusing ones — all of which helped shape how he thinks today.

If you’re a student reading this: it’s completely normal to feel lost sometimes. Most people you think have it all sorted… don’t.

sections.title: Life Outside Screens
sections.content:
Outside work, Shashwat is not constantly thinking about code or AI. He has painted in the past (including wall paintings), enjoys watching movies and shows, listens to music almost all the time, and likes slowing life down occasionally.

He enjoys science fiction and mystery movies and shows, and appreciates good storytelling — the kind that makes you think a little after it ends.

He also played sports growing up, from cricket in childhood to squash in college. These days it’s less about competition and more about staying active and balanced.

sections.title: Poker, Overthinking & Questionable Decisions
sections.content:
Shashwat is a big fan of poker. During college, poker nights in the hostel were a regular thing. It was less about winning and more about strategy, probability, psychology, and having fun.

Poker appealed to him because it mirrors real life in strange ways — you make the best decision you can with incomplete information and still don’t always win.

Also, yes, there was a lot of overthinking involved.

sections.title: Travel, Mountains & Saying Yes to Plans
sections.content:
Shashwat is a mountain person. He grew up around mountains in Jammu, and that love never really went away. He enjoys trekking, hiking, and being in places that make you feel small in a good way.

He has traveled across India — from Jammu and Kashmir to Kerala — and is usually up for trips, spontaneous plans, or just exploring somewhere new.

If someone says “let’s travel,” there’s a good chance he’ll say yes.

sections.title: Random Curiosity & Overthinking
sections.content:
Shashwat is naturally curious. He enjoys reading about new technology, space, science, and ideas that don’t always have immediate practical value.

Sometimes this curiosity turns into deep thinking. Sometimes it just turns into random rabbit holes on the internet.

Both are acceptable outcomes.

sections.title: If You Want to Say Hi
sections.content:
If you’re a student, a friend, or someone who just randomly landed here and found this interesting — you can reach out.

Shashwat is generally open to conversations, questions, or random messages (as long as they’re human). Whether it’s about college, AI, travel, or just curiosity, it’s okay to say hi.

sections.title: Wrong Place for Serious Questions (And That’s Okay)
sections.content:
If you’re here, you’re probably exploring, scrolling, or just casually stalking the site — and that’s exactly what this profile is for. This space is meant to be fun, relatable, and a mix of personal life with a light touch of what Shashwat does professionally.

Sometimes though, curiosity naturally turns into more serious questions. If you start wondering about things like:

• Detailed explanations of his work or projects
• How specific AI systems or platforms were designed
• Technical architecture, code, or implementation details
• Career advice, hiring decisions, or interview-related topics
• His academic background, achievements, or professional milestones

Then this profile will only give you partial answers — on purpose.

👉 If you want clear, professional, and impact-focused answers, switch to the **Recruiter profile**.
👉 If you want deep technical details, engineering decisions, or system-level explanations, switch to the **Developer profile**.

This Stalker profile is for curiosity, not credentials. Feel free to hang around — and when you want something more serious, the right profile is just one click away.
